directAnswer: GPU crashes under load can be caused by overheating, power supply issues, or driver conflicts.
summary: Understanding the common causes of GPU crashes can help in troubleshooting and preventing future occurrences.

sections.heading: Overheating
sections.body: GPUs can overheat due to dust buildup in fans, inadequate cooling solutions, or high ambient temperatures. Monitoring GPU temperatures using tools like MSI Afterburner can help identify overheating issues.

sections.heading: Power Supply Issues
sections.body: An insufficient or failing power supply can lead to GPU crashes under load. Ensure your PSU meets the wattage requirements of your GPU and check for any signs of damage.

sections.heading: Driver Conflicts
sections.body: Outdated or corrupted drivers can cause instability. Regularly updating your GPU drivers from the manufacturer's website can help maintain stability.

steps.title: Check GPU Temperature
steps.detail: Use monitoring software like MSI Afterburner or HWMonitor to check if the GPU temperature exceeds safe limits (usually above 85°C).

steps.title: Inspect Power Supply
steps.detail: Verify that your power supply unit (PSU) provides adequate wattage for your GPU and check for any visible damage or wear.

steps.title: Update Graphics Drivers
steps.detail: Visit the GPU manufacturer's website (NVIDIA, AMD) to download and install the latest drivers.

steps.title: Clean GPU and Case
steps.detail: Dust can obstruct airflow, so clean your GPU and case fans regularly to ensure proper cooling.

faqs.question: What are the signs of a failing GPU?
faqs.answer: Signs of a failing GPU include graphical artifacts, crashes during gaming, and failure to boot.

faqs.question: How can I improve GPU cooling?
faqs.answer: Improving GPU cooling can be achieved by ensuring good airflow in your case, using aftermarket coolers, or adding additional case fans.

faqs.question: Is it safe to overclock my GPU?
faqs.answer: Overclocking can increase performance but also raises the risk of overheating and instability. Always monitor temperatures and stability after overclocking.

caveats: Symptoms may vary based on specific hardware configurations and software environments.
